title: On-Policy & Off-Policy Distillation — Post-Training as Distribution Matching

authoring_notes.purpose: A focused, research-altitude course on how large language models are distilled: the difference between OFF-policy distillation (train the student on a fixed set of teacher outputs) and ON-policy distillation (the student samples its own trajectories and a fixed teacher grades every token), why the on-policy property matters, and when each wins. The course is grounded in a crawl-assembled library of primary sources: the Thinking Machines 'On-Policy Distillation' blog and nrehiew's 'SFT vs RL vs OPD' blog (quoted verbatim), plus the canonical papers (Hinton KD, Kim & Rush sequence-level KD, Ross et al DAgger, Agarwal et al GKD, Gu et al MiniLLM, the Qwen3 technical report) and the practical TRL/HuggingFace recipe (thesis-extracted / doc-quoted). The capstone designs an on-policy-distillation strategy for the learner's real SFT data pipeline at /Users/jaewon/mywork_2026/Lina_2026/boson-agent-synthetic-data-dev.
authoring_notes.framing: This is a DISTRIBUTION-MATCHING course. The single organizing idea, from nrehiew and Thinking Machines: every post-training method (SFT, RL, distillation) reshapes the model's sequence distribution, and they differ on three axes — (1) DATA SOURCE: off-policy (data from teacher/dataset) vs on-policy (data sampled from the student itself); (2) SIGNAL DENSITY: sparse O(1) bits/episode (RL scalar reward) vs dense O(N) bits/episode (per-token teacher signal); (3) DIVERGENCE GEOMETRY: forward KL (mode-covering, SFT) vs reverse KL (mode-seeking, RL/OPD). On-policy distillation is the corner of this cube that combines 'the density of distillation, the unbiasedness of RL, and the on-policy property of both' (nrehiew). Every chapter is priced as a bet: what does this method buy, and what does it cost (teacher-logprob access, sampling infra, entropy-collapse risk)?
authoring_notes.why_this_learner: UC Berkeley EECS; career goal is model-architecture / post-training research at Anthropic; already fluent in SFT/RL from an active llm-training course (synthetic -> SFT -> RL tracks, currently ~ch-21). Skip math scaffolding but DO give real equations and quote primary sources verbatim, not paraphrase (the learner explicitly wants core insight + real source text). Research-framing-priority and forward-skip-prone: land every concept on the payoff, which here is a concrete design for his own conversation-data SFT pipeline (boson-agent-synthetic-data-dev). Lead the learner to WHY (causal reasoning), push back on definitional 'what' answers. Present each method as a priced bet, never a best practice.
authoring_notes.structure: 7 chapters in 6 phases. foundations (ch-01) installs the distribution-matching map (the three axes, forward vs reverse KL). off-policy (ch-02) covers classical distillation as the baseline the course improves on: Hinton soft targets -> Kim & Rush sequence-level KD, both off-policy. on-policy-core (ch-03..ch-04): ch-03 installs the exposure-bias / compounding-error problem (Ross DAgger) and the on-policy principle as its cure; ch-04 is the heart — the on-policy distillation mechanism (student samples, teacher grades each token, per-token reverse KL) unified across the Thinking Machines blog, Agarwal GKD, and MiniLLM reverse-KL. tradeoffs (ch-05) prices it: the compute numbers, when it wins vs RL/SFT, per-token clipping, entropy collapse, 'data source matters more than teacher'. practice (ch-06) is the implementation reference (TRL GKDTrainer, the HF 'any model family' recipe, teacher-logprob serving). capstone (ch-07) is a LAB: an on-policy-distillation strategy memo for the boson-agent conversation-data SFT pipeline, then a live strategy discussion. Dependencies are strictly sequential; no chapter depends on a later one.
authoring_notes.per_chapter_format: Each read.md must (1) QUOTE the real primary sources via [[excerpt-slug]] wikilinks — reproduce verbatim quotes from the blogs/docs exactly as the excerpt records them, and clearly mark paper theses that were extracted rather than fetched verbatim; (2) extract the chapter's Core Insight + one practitioner Guideline; (3) give the real math where it clarifies (temperature-softmax, forward vs reverse KL, the per-token reverse-KL objective, the GKD generalized-JSD/lambda knobs) — the learner wants equations, not hand-waving; (4) surface the relevant doc-vs-reality myth and resolve it with the primary source; (5) price the method as a bet — what it keeps cheap (sample efficiency, exposure-bias reduction) and what it costs (teacher-logprob access, sampling infra, collapse risk); (6) connect at least one move back to the boson-agent conversation-data SFT pipeline. Each chapter MUST emit a self-contained companion HTML visualization under ch-XX/figures/ (inline CSS/JS, no external CDNs, renders offline) at the point in the prose where it most helps — candidates: a forward-vs-reverse-KL mode-covering/mode-seeking animation; a compounding-error/exposure-bias trajectory-drift explorer; an SFT/RL/OPD three-axis cube; a per-token teacher-grading walkthrough over a sampled sequence; a compute-cost (OPD vs RL vs SFT) bar/curve; a GKD lambda/beta parameter explorer; a boson-pipeline OPD data-flow diagram. Each chapter MUST end with an '## Additional Reading' section listing the real papers/blogs/docs (with URLs) beyond the cited excerpts. Markdown + wikilinks is the backbone; HTML amplifies.
authoring_notes.depth_target: Source-rich and long (match the software-arch / llm-training chapters). Every mechanism claim is backed by a quoted primary source or a clearly-marked paper thesis from the excerpts. Real equations included. Where the popular narrative and the primary source disagree, the primary source wins and the myth is named.
authoring_notes.reconciliation_myths_by_chapter: ch-01: 'distillation = train a small model to copy a big one' (that is only OFF-policy KD; on-policy distillation grades the student's OWN rollouts). ch-02: 'SFT and distillation are different things' (SFT on teacher-generated data IS off-policy sequence-level distillation). ch-03: 'more teacher data fixes imitation learning' (no — exposure bias is a distribution-shift problem; the fix is on-policy data, DAgger's O(T) vs behavioral cloning's O(T^2)). ch-04: 'on-policy distillation is just a kind of RL' (it is on-policy LIKE RL but dense like distillation — the reward is the teacher's per-token logprob, O(N) bits, not a sparse scalar) + 'reverse vs forward KL is a detail' (reverse KL is what makes OPD mode-seeking and 'unhackable'). ch-05: 'on-policy distillation is always better' (no — math/code often favor RL; it needs teacher-logprob access; entropy-collapse risk). ch-06: 'the student and teacher must share a tokenizer/family' (the HF H4 recipe unlocks cross-family on-policy distillation). ch-07: capstone — 'the boson pipeline is already on-policy' (the CUSTOMER simulator samples on-policy, but the SELLER student is trained OFF-policy on generated transcripts; that is the gap OPD closes).
authoring_notes.capstone_target_notes: boson-agent-synthetic-data-dev generates multi-turn Korean insurance TMR (tele-sales) conversations: a scenario-driven customer (sampled live from a rotation of 11 models incl. Claude Haiku, GPT-5-mini, Grok, Gemini, and 6 Qwen/boson variants) talks to a stage-puppeted seller (test-lina, boson Qwen3.6-27B). Output = dual-view clean JSON + raw JSONL preserving tool_use/tool_result blocks and pre/post-compaction snapshots. It is DATA-GENERATION ONLY (v0.14): no reward, no RL, no distillation loop; the Lina seller checkpoints (Qwen3.6-27B-Lina-chk-*) are SFT'd on these transcripts — i.e. trained OFF-policy. The capstone's thesis: 20-50-turn agent dialogue is exactly the long-horizon compounding-error regime where off-policy SFT diverges, and OPD is the targeted fix — have the student SELLER sample its own turns within the fixed scenario skeleton and let a strong teacher (Claude / large Qwen) grade each token by reverse KL. The lab must handle: which turns/tokens to grade (assistant seller turns, incl. tool-call tokens), compaction boundaries, barge-in cuts, the teacher-logprob-serving cost, and disambiguating the pipeline's existing 'on-policy' customer sampling from on-policy training of the seller.

chapters.title: Post-Training as Distribution Matching: SFT, RL, and Distillation on One Map
concepts: The spine: every post-training method reshapes the model's sequence distribution; they differ on three axes — data source (on/off-policy), signal density (sparse O(1) vs dense O(N) bits/episode), and divergence geometry (forward vs reverse KL) ([[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]], [[tm-on-policy-distillation]])
SFT = fixed external target distribution, cross-entropy = forward KL, mode-covering, no built-in anti-forgetting regularization ([[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]])

RL = no external target, reward-direction updates on on-policy samples only, 'learns the nearest task-solving policy'; dense-vs-sparse: 'RL only teaches O(1) bits per episode… distillation teaches O(N) bits' ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]], [[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]])

Forward KL (mode-covering) vs reverse KL (mode-seeking) with equations; why the geometry decides whether prior capabilities are preserved or averaged away ([[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]], [[gu-minillm-reverse-kd]])

The thesis that names the target corner: 'You want something with the density of distillation, the unbiasedness of RL, and the on-policy property of both' — on-policy distillation is that corner ([[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]])

Myth killed: 'distillation just means training a small model to copy a big one' — that is only OFF-policy KD; on-policy distillation grades the student's OWN rollouts. Applied: locate the boson SFT pipeline on this map (dense, off-policy imitation of generated transcripts)

chapters.title: Off-Policy Distillation: From Hinton Soft Targets to Sequence-Level KD
concepts: Classical knowledge distillation (Hinton, Vinyals, Dean 2015): soft targets carry 'dark knowledge'; temperature-softened softmax q_i = exp(z_i/T)/sum_j exp(z_j/T); the distillation loss = weighted soft-target CE (at temperature T) + hard-label CE ([[hinton-knowledge-distillation]])

Why soft targets beat hard labels: the teacher's full probability vector carries far more bits per example than a one-hot label — the seed of the O(N)-bits idea ([[hinton-knowledge-distillation]], [[tm-on-policy-distillation]])
Sequence-level KD (Kim & Rush 2016): move from per-word soft labels to training the student on the teacher's GENERATED output sequences; sequence-level interpolation; NMT results ([[kim-rush-seqkd]])

The defining limitation shared by both: the data comes from the TEACHER (or a fixed dataset), so the student only ever learns in teacher-visited contexts — this is OFF-policy distillation ([[kim-rush-seqkd]], [[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]])

Myth killed: 'SFT and distillation are different things' — SFT on teacher-generated sequences IS off-policy sequence-level distillation; the boundary is the data source, not the loss name ([[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]])

Applied: the current boson seller-student (Qwen3.6-27B-Lina-chk-*) is SFT'd on generated transcripts = textbook off-policy sequence-level KD; set up why that will compound error over long calls (paid off in ch-03)

chapters.title: Exposure Bias and the On-Policy Principle: DAgger at Token Level
concepts: Exposure bias / compounding error (Ross, Gordon, Bagnell 2011, DAgger): a policy trained on the expert's state distribution drifts into states the expert never visited; behavioral cloning has O(T^2) error in the horizon T vs O(T) for on-policy ([[ross-dagger-exposure-bias]])

The autoregressive translation: 'because of autoregression, one mistake by the student might move it to states the teacher would have never visited' — acute for long sequences ([[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]], [[tm-on-policy-distillation]])

DAgger's fix = collect training data by running the STUDENT policy and labeling its visited states with the expert's action — an ON-POLICY data-collection loop; on-policy distillation is this move applied at token level ([[ross-dagger-exposure-bias]], [[tm-on-policy-distillation]])

'The strength of on-policy training is that by training on samples from itself, the student learns to avoid mistakes in a more direct way' — the student is graded exactly in the states it will actually reach ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]])

RL as on-policy-but-sparse; the continual-learning subtlety: SFT on a model's own samples still drifts off-policy over finite batches, degrading instruction-following — on-policy distillation stays aligned throughout ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]], [[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]])

Myth killed: 'more teacher data fixes imitation learning' — no; exposure bias is a distribution-shift problem, not a data-quantity problem. Applied: 20-50-turn TMR sales dialogue is a long horizon where the SFT'd seller compounds error the moment it deviates from a teacher-visited path

chapters.title: On-Policy Distillation: Dense Teacher Signal on Student Rollouts
concepts: The mechanism (Thinking Machines): the student samples its OWN trajectories and a fixed high-performing teacher grades EACH token; per-token reverse KL objective KL(pi_theta || pi_teacher) = E_{x~pi_theta}[log pi_theta(x_{t+1}|x_{1..t}) - log pi_teacher(x_{t+1}|x_{1..t})] ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]])

Why reverse KL is 'unhackable' and mode-seeking: low KL always means high probability of desirable teacher behavior; 'when the student behaves identically to the teacher, reverse KL is zero' ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]], [[gu-minillm-reverse-kd]])

The 4-step implementation: (1) init teacher client; (2) sample student trajectories + capture student logprobs; (3) query teacher compute_logprobs on those trajectories; (4) set per-token advantage = negative reverse KL and reuse the RL importance-sampling loss ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]])

The academic generalization — GKD (Agarwal et al 2024): train on self-generated sequences with token-level teacher feedback; the lambda knob (fraction of on-policy student data) and a generalized-JSD/beta knob interpolating forward<->reverse KL; on-policy/mixed data beats fixed-dataset KD ([[agarwal-gkd]])

Reverse-KL distillation for LLMs (MiniLLM, Gu et al 2024): policy-gradient optimization of KL(student||teacher) so the student is mode-seeking on open-ended generation — the same geometry the TM recipe uses ([[gu-minillm-reverse-kd]])

Myths killed: 'on-policy distillation is just RL' (it is on-policy like RL but dense like distillation — reward = teacher per-token logprob, O(N) bits) and 'forward vs reverse KL is a detail'. Applied: OPD as the seller-student's training objective inside the fixed scenario skeleton

chapters.title: Economics and Failure Modes: When On-Policy Distillation Wins
concepts: The compute case (Qwen3 report, Table 21): SFT-400K -> 60% AIME24; +RL 17,920 GPU-hrs -> 67.6%; +on-policy-distillation 1,800 GPU-hrs -> 74.4% — a ~10x cost reduction vs RL at a HIGHER score ([[qwen3-strong-to-weak-distillation]], [[tm-on-policy-distillation]])

Further efficiency: 9-30x vs SFT-scaling (FLOPs), and self-distillation reaching teacher performance in 7-10x fewer gradient steps / 50-100x compute due to shorter contexts and smaller batches ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]])

When it wins: long sequences, continual learning / personalization recovery (mid-training on internal docs tanks IF-eval; OPD restores it without losing new knowledge), and distilling a specialized teacher's behavior cheaply ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]])

Failure modes and knobs: entropy collapse ('drastic collapse in entropy' with sudden reward jumps), per-token clipping because style tokens ('wait','alright') carry higher KL than task-critical tokens, and the finding that 'the source of the data matters a lot while the teacher matters less than expected' ([[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]], [[tm-on-policy-distillation]])
Domain dependence: math/code often favor RL; creative-writing and knowledge tasks favor distillation because reward signals are noisier there ([[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]])

Myth killed: 'on-policy distillation is always better'. Price the bet: OPD requires teacher-logprob access + student-sampling infra and risks collapse; name what it buys (exposure-bias reduction, sample efficiency) vs costs. Applied: is a 20-50-turn sales call the regime where OPD's long-horizon advantage pays for the teacher-serving cost?

chapters.title: Practical Recipes: GKD in TRL and On-Policy Distillation for Any Model Family
concepts: TRL GKDTrainer as the reference implementation: the key args — lmbda (fraction of on-policy student-generated data), beta (generalized-JSD interpolation between forward and reverse KL), temperature — mapped back to the ch-04 mechanism ([[hf-trl-gkd-recipe]], [[agarwal-gkd]])

The HuggingFace H4 'Unlocking On-Policy Distillation for Any Model Family' recipe: the cross-tokenizer / cross-family challenge and how the recipe lets a teacher from a different family grade a student's rollouts ([[hf-trl-gkd-recipe]])

Serving teacher logprobs: the practical bottleneck is a forward pass of the teacher over the student's samples (compute_logprobs); on-policy sampling loop + teacher grading in a single training step ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]], [[hf-trl-gkd-recipe]])

Hyperparameter reality: temperature, lambda schedule (how much on-policy vs fixed data), beta choice (reverse-KL-leaning for mode-seeking), and batch/context sizing that make OPD cheap ([[hf-trl-gkd-recipe]], [[tm-on-policy-distillation]])

Pitfalls in practice: tokenizer mismatch, teacher-serving cost, entropy collapse mitigation, and verifying the student is graded on its OWN samples (not silently drifting to off-policy) ([[hf-trl-gkd-recipe]], [[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]])
Myth killed: 'the student and teacher must share a tokenizer/family'. Applied: which teacher (Claude vs large Qwen) and which serving path fit the boson pipeline's multilingual, tool-calling seller

chapters.title: Capstone Lab: On-Policy Distillation Strategy for the boson-agent Conversation-Data SFT Pipeline
concepts: Map the pipeline onto the distribution cube: the customer simulator already samples ON-policy (11-model rotation), but the SELLER student (Qwen3.6-27B-Lina-chk-*) is trained OFF-policy on generated transcripts — the exposure-bias gap OPD closes ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]], [[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]], [[ross-dagger-exposure-bias]])

The long-horizon argument: 20-50-turn TMR sales calls are the compounding-error regime of ch-03; a seller that deviates early (a mishandled objection, a bad barge-in recovery) drifts into states no transcript covered — exactly where dense per-token teacher grading on the student's OWN turns helps most

Concrete design: student seller samples its turns within the FIXED scenario skeleton (stages, personas, barge-ins) while a teacher (Claude or a large Qwen) grades each seller-turn token by reverse KL; reuse the existing relay/orchestrator as the on-policy rollout environment ([[tm-on-policy-distillation]], [[agarwal-gkd]], [[hf-trl-gkd-recipe]])

The hard parts: which tokens to grade (assistant seller turns incl. tool_use tokens vs skip customer/tool_result), compaction boundaries (pre/post snapshots), barge-in dual-cuts, and whether to grade in Korean with a cross-family teacher (ties to ch-06's any-model-family recipe)

Price the bet for THIS system: teacher-logprob serving cost + sampling infra vs exposure-bias reduction over long calls; where OPD sits relative to a cheaper SFT-refresh or a full RL reward model (closure rate / compliance) ([[qwen3-strong-to-weak-distillation]], [[nrehiew-sft-rl-opd]])
Deliverable: an OPD strategy memo for boson-agent-synthetic-data-dev (what to sample, what to grade, which teacher, what to measure) + a live strategy discussion — the research-framing payoff
